title: Edge-prefilter + periodic resample controller to minimize tracing hotpath allocations
creator: Marisol Chen
description:
Problem: recent sampling improvements reduced trace volume but a few regressions still cause high allocation and CPU pressure in the ingress hotpath when doing span encoding/decision work. This affects tail latency for high-QPS endpoints and increases cost on allocated pods. Goal: introduce a low-cost edge-prefilter to make an early accept/skip decision for the tracing hotpath, and pair it with a background periodic resample controller that rescues missed tail candidates without blocking the hot request path.

Proposed approach: 1) Edge-prefilter: implement a tiny fingerprint + heuristics check in the ingress proxy (C++/Rust module) that inspects request headers and light metadata only, computing a 16-bit sketch to cheaply identify likely-to-be-uninteresting requests. The prefilter returns a triage decision: skip-hotpath, record-light-metadata, or defer-to-full-sampler. The code path must avoid allocations and should be implemented with stack buffers and branch-friendly hot paths. 2) Periodic resample controller: a background worker (k8s CronJob / controller) consumes compact telemetry logs (small wire-format) and re-evaluates deferred traces with the heavier tail-sampling logic (full payload permitted off-hotpath). If a deferred trace is promoted (tail candidate), the controller requests the full span payload from a short-lived buffer store and commits the trace to the tracing backend. 3) Observability + eval: add shadow mode to record both decisions, and instrument new metrics (prefilter_reject_ratio, deferred_promote_rate, hotpath_alloc_bytes/request, ingress_tracer_cpu). Compare before/after using the perf dashboard.

Trade-offs and constraints: - Risk of missed tail candidates if prefilter is too aggressive. Mitigation: conservative default thresholds and short buffer retention to enable promotion. - Extra complexity in the background controller and buffer store (latency/consistency). Use TTL-backed ephemeral storage limited to 30s. - Needs careful on-host resource accounting to avoid swapping cost to background job.

Rollout plan: 1) Implement prefilter in a feature-flagged build and enable shadow mode for 10% of non-prod traffic. 2) Run stress benchmarks (see links) and internal dogfood for 2 weeks. 3) Canary to 5% of production with lambda-based quick rollback. 4) Gradual ramp to 50%+ after meeting metrics. 5) Enable full promote path and consider default-on for low-risk tenants.

Success criteria (measurable): - Hotpath allocations per request reduced by >=40% for sampled endpoints. - Ingress tracing CPU down by >=25% at 95th traffic scenario. - Deferred promote rate yields coverage of >=99% for errors classified sev1/2 within 30s retention window. - No increase in p99 API latency beyond 2ms.

Testing and validation: microbenchmarks for allocation and branch misses, e2e load tests with synthetic tail errors, integration tests for promotion correctness, and a 72-hour canary with continuous regression alerts.

Open tasks / next steps: - Finalize prefilter sketch format (Mar 15) - PR for ingress proxy changes (in review) - Implement ephemeral buffer store with size quotas - Add dashboard panels and alert rules - Prepare rollout runbook and rollback steps

Related notes: this approach intentionally separates decision work from heavier sampling evaluation and rehydration to preserve hotpath latency while keeping high fidelity for tails via background promotion.
